note: The pairs a split promises to read on every run. A pair is a claim that two arms differ only by the lever named between them, so it can be read inside one artifact on the same questions by the same judge — which is the only reading of a delta this repository accepts. The placement pair is here because it was published the other way: `synth-definitions` and `inline-definitions` were compared across two runs (41.4 against 45.0) and written into the benchmark document as +3.6pp, and inside a single run they are 18 and 17 discordant cases with p = 1.0000 (run 42491745712). The audit pair is here because its `+1.01pp at p = 0.27` is a reading every later round quotes and none re-derives. The selector pair is here because the arm that decides adoption spends four calls a case and the question `metadata+evidence -> select` is what those calls buy. `inline+evidence -> metadata+evidence` is here because it decides the product claim — a database with no documentation reaching one that has it — and it is the only pair whose two splits disagree: dev read it at +0.07pp (65:66, p = 1.0000, run 41296610389) and Mini-Dev's three-run pool reads +2.89pp ± 1.55 (p < 0.001), on 496 of dev's own questions. A split with no entry declares nothing: an empty list is a statement, and it is the honest one for a split whose decision is not a delta. The dev split declares three pairs rather than five because it runs five arms; the five Mini-Dev pairs include the placement pair, which the dev run does not score.
